messages.author: cac9c48e94a4f3f7
messages.subject: Multilevel SEM - Lavaan limitations
parts:
Dear all,

I'm aware, just like mentioned in lavaan documentation (https://lavaan.ugent.be/tutorial/multilevel.html) that multilevel SEM in lavaan is for now limited to two-level analysis with continuous data. But I'm not sure how to interpret this. My question is on whether we can have ordinal data at the individual level and only continuous data at the second level, or if BOTH levels must only have continuous data.

I've tested an SEM model using some scales - latent variables - and considering its items as ordinal data (estimator was WLSMV) at the individual level, which works fine and has interesting patterns, but I'd like to add three class-level (2nd level) continuous variables to account for its role on the analyzed model. Is this possible with lavaan, or my only option would be to use MplusAutomation and adapt to Mplus syntax?

I appreciate any help.
Best,
Mafalda.

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Multilevel SEM - Lavaan limitations
parts: whether we can have ordinal data at the individual level and only continuous data at the second level, or if BOTH levels must only have continuous data.

Only continuous variables are supported for MLSEM.
 
Is this possible with lavaan

lavaan only supports 2-level MLSEMs.  The only way to incorporate a third level is in wide format, like a growth curve model.
